title: Chapter 9: Scared to Tears
html:
“Senior, why do I feel like these paper mannequins are watching us?” He San clutched the doorframe and refused to enter. “I’m serious! Something is wrong with them. What if they’re actually people in disguise? F*ck, I feel like they’re going to start moving any second!”

There was something uncanny about the paper mannequins Chen Ge had touched up with Mortician’s Makeup. They were obviously inanimate, yet they possessed an unsettling hint of life.

Gao Ru Xue glared angrily at He San. She thought to herself, Why did I bring him with me today?! Fear is contagious. I wasn’t that nervous at first, but now even he’s starting to get to me.

“Would you keep those thoughts to yourself? If you make one more useless observation like that, I’m leaving you here.”

She entered first and gave the room a quick inspection. The Main House windows were purely decorative and did not lead outside.

“Senior, let’s go. This building is saturated with yin energy, and it’s sealed up tight. The exit definitely isn’t here.”

“The owner understands human psychology and knows how to manipulate expectations, so we should do the opposite of what an ordinary visitor would do. A place that looks as though it couldn’t possibly contain the exit is exactly where we should search more carefully.” Gao Ru Xue walked around the room. The air stirred by her movements made several fallen paper mannequins scrape faintly across the floor.

He San remained outside the door with his heart in his throat. “But there’s nowhere to hide anything in that room. You can see every surface. Where could an exit possibly be?”

“Nowhere to hide anything? Who told you that?” Gao Ru Xue stopped in the center of the room and planted one foot against the red coffin. “Come help me. We’re opening this coffin.”

“Open that?!” He San’s pale lips trembled. “Isn’t that a little disrespectful?”

“Do you plan to spend the rest of your life in this Haunted House?” After repeated urging from Gao Ru Xue, He San inched farther into the room, keeping as much distance as possible from the paper mannequins. Finally, he bent down and took hold of one side of the coffin lid.

“On the count of three, pull!”

“Okay.”

“One, two…”

“Dong!” Gao Ru Xue had only made it halfway through the countdown when a loud thud echoed through the room.

“What was that?” He San nearly jumped out of his skin.

“Shush!” Gao Ru Xue raised a finger to her lips. She looked around before her gaze settled on the red coffin. “I think the sound came from inside.”

At those words, the color drained from He San’s face. His throat bobbed, and his hands trembled on the coffin lid. “Senior, I’m begging you. There’s nothing here. Can we please go?”

“Calm down. The sound only happened when we were about to open the lid. Don’t you think that’s suspicious?”

“Senior, the coffin just made a noise. That’s a lot more than suspicious!” Under the influence of Black Friday, He San’s fear had grown steadily stronger; by now, he wanted nothing more than to leave.

“Think about it. There are only two likely explanations. Either an employee is hiding in there waiting to scare us, or there’s some hidden mechanism that activates when the coffin is opened. Either way, the coffin is important to the scenario. If we want to find the exit, we need to open it.” Gao Ru Xue slapped the lid twice. “Stop hesitating. Pull.”

“I have no idea whether any of that is true, but it sounded convincing.”

He San and Gao Ru Xue pulled together, and the heavy coffin lid began to slide aside. When it was about a quarter open, the ancient-looking coffin suddenly burst open with a deafening bang.

Paper mannequins and paper money erupted from the coffin as a strange woman’s laugh filled the room. At the same moment, the Main House door began closing on its own.

“Let’s get out before it’s too late!” He San did not hesitate. Because he was closest to the entrance, panic made him forget his senior completely. He dashed toward the door, but before he could reach it, a woman’s face suddenly appeared in front of him.

The face was deathly pale yet strikingly beautiful.

“F*ck!” He San’s first instinct was to swing at the face, but its owner seemed to anticipate him and easily twisted out of reach.

“Ghost! Help!” He San dropped to the floor, then scrambled away on hands and feet before breaking into a run.

“He San! Stop running around blindly!” Gao Ru Xue shouted when she saw a red shadow follow him into the building he had fled into.

“The side houses belonged to the sons and daughters. This is bad—the room He San entered was the specter’s living quarters before she died!” Gao Ru Xue rushed for the exit only to find the door locked. She pounded on the wood and cursed. “Divide and conquer? It’s just a Haunted House! Do you really have to go this far?!”

The coffin had broken apart, and paper mannequins littered the floor. Trapped inside, Gao Ru Xue finally lost her composure. She hammered at the door until it opened a minute later.

Yet in that single minute, everything outside the Main House seemed to have changed.

“Xiao San? He San!” Gao Ru Xue called twice, but no one answered. Apart from the eerie background music, the only response was the soft rustle of paper money brushing across the floor.

What’s going on? This Haunted House isn’t that big. There’s no way He San didn’t hear me. Did something happen to him?For reasons Gao Ru Xue could not explain, the image of a crime scene flashed through her mind. She retraced her steps along the corridor until she reached the West House.Xiao San ran this way earlier.

The old wooden door creaked open, and celebratory calligraphy written on white paper fluttered to the floor. Gao Ru Xue stepped into what looked like a bridal chamber, but instead of auspicious red, every decoration was white—the traditional color of mourning. The effect was deeply unsettling.

Where has he run off to?Something about the room felt wrong. Its only light came from the white lantern hanging outside the door. Gao Ru Xue moved forward slowly while cold drafts blew in behind her, sending a chill across her exposed skin.

Paper money crunched beneath her feet. Every so often, her shoe struck something hard that she could not identify in the darkness. Gritting her teeth, she pressed on.

Gao Ru Xue pulled open the curtains to let in more light. The room was empty except for a bed concealed behind layers of mosquito netting and a pair of bronze mirrors facing each other near the wall.

I saw He San run into this room with my own eyes. Only a minute or two has passed. He couldn’t have disappeared that quickly… Unless the exit is in here and he stumbled across it by accident?

Gao Ru Xue took a deep breath and decided to inspect the room more carefully. The moment she took her first step, however, she heard another set of footsteps directly behind her.

“Who’s behind me?”

She spun around, but there was nothing behind her except a bronze mirror and her own reflection.
